newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU fears channel transport duopoly.
newsitem.headline: EU fears channel transport duopoly.

text.p: The European Commission is concerned that a link between the Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company (P&0) and Stena line AB of Sweden may create a duopoly in cross-channel transport, EU sources said on Thursday.
"The major fear...is the risk of a duopoly situation between Le Shuttle and this outfit," one source said. Le Shuttle operates car train services through the channel tunneloperated by Eurotunnel.
The sources said the Commission understood that British merger authorities investigating the deal had the same concerns.
But "it is the decision by the European Commission that prevails."
Earlier, EU sources said the Commission's competition service has drafted a "letter of serious doubts" about the deal, which would merge the two companies' cross-Channel ferry operations.

The final decision on whether to send the letter must be taken by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert in consultation with Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock and the Commission's legal service, one of the sources said.
"It is not certain that the Commission will send the letter; it has until June 11 to do it," the source told Reuters.
Van Miert usually follows his services' advice.

Under EU rules covering corporate agreements in the shipping sector, the Commission has until next Wednesday to raise any objections or the planned link-up between P&O and Stena will get an automatic six-year exemption from EU competition rules.
If the Commission does indeed raise problems, the exemption could be reduced or the deal could be blocked if the companies do not offer any remedies.
The sources played down the announcement earlier this week by Stena that the French authorities, which are also investigating the deal, had given the green light.
"What the French said was we let this go, but we will be watching this carefully in a number of points," one source said.
There is no deadline for the Commission to come to a final ruling if the EU investigation goes beyond next week.
P&O and Stena Line said on Thursday they were still confident the joint venture would go ahead.
"We are not expecting any major delay" a P&O spokesman told Reuters in London.
"Neither P&O nor us have any indications that it will not go through," Stena spokesman Mats King told Reuters in Stockholm.
